111:
§1. Through the reception of baptism, a child of parents who belong to the Latin Church is enrolled in it. If one parent does not belong to it, the child is enrolled in the Latin Church if both parents have jointly chosen baptism there. If they do not agree, the child is enrolled in the Church sui iuris to which the father belongs.

§2. If only one parent is Catholic, the child is enrolled in the Church to which that Catholic parent belongs.

§3. Anyone to be baptized who has completed fourteen years of age may freely choose baptism in the Latin Church or another Church sui iuris, and belongs to the Church chosen.
868:
§1. For an infant to be baptized lawfully:

1° the parents, at least one parent, or the person who lawfully takes their place must consent;

2° there must be a founded hope that the infant will be brought up in the Catholic religion, without prejudice to §3. If such hope is entirely lacking, baptism is to be deferred according to particular law, after the parents have been informed of the reason.

§2. An infant of Catholic parents, and even of non-Catholic parents, may lawfully be baptized in danger of death even against the parents’ will.

§3. An infant of non-Catholic Christians may lawfully be baptized if the parents, at least one parent, or the person who lawfully takes their place requests it and it is physically or morally impossible for them to approach their own minister.
